Subject: Multiplex tenancy QoS & SLA matrix — VPC/private GPU handoff

Hi Maria / Helios ops team, and internal infra leads,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As discussed, this thread is the working handoff for the private deployment sizing and QoS gating for the multi-tenant GPU pool you will host in your VPC (bare metal k8s + SR-IOV NICs). Attachments: multiplex_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx (per-tenant qps/throughput targets + prioritization) and net_qos_playbook_v2.pdf (recommended VLAN/QoS markings and MTU/NIC tuning).

High-level ask from Helios: support three tenant classes with distinct throughput & tail latency SLOs while preserving isolation during surges. We propose the following baseline commitments for the first 6 months so we can iterate: 
- Gold tenants: 500 sustained infer/sec, p95 token latency <= 180ms, burst to 1.2k/sec for 3m windows
- Silver tenants: 150 sustained infer/sec, p95 token latency <= 300ms, burst to 400/sec for 3m windows
- Bronze tenants: 25 sustained infer/sec, best-effort latency target <= 500ms, burst to 100/sec

Sizing assumptions (see sheet 'Sizing'): quantized LLaMA-derived model, avg request 120 tokens, KV cache warm for 70% of interactive traffic, effective batching 12 tokens per batch on Ampere A100-equivalent; ~32 concurrent Gold sessions map to 1 GPU slot under sustained load. Network: reserve 8Gbps per host for egress (model weights streaming + embeddings offload) and mark tenant flows with DSCP EF/AF for prioritization.

Operational controls we want in place before first canary: 
- Admission control policy: strict backpressure for Bronze during Gold surge (circuit-breaker at node-level)
- Tenant-weighted fair queuing on the egress NVMe / NIC path (SR-IOV VF-level policing)
- Prefix/KV cache partitioning per-tenant where possible to reduce noisy-neighbor eviction
- Autoscale policy: scale-up on sustained 85% GPU util across pool for 90s, scale-down after 10m of <40% util with staged deallocation to keep warm caches

Open questions for Helios ops: 
1) Can you confirm per-host NIC hardware and whether SR-IOV is enabled across the candidate fleet?
2) What circuit limits do you expect from the cloud provider / datacenter egress (BGP / firewall shaping)?
3) Do you have an existing VLAN plan we should align DSCP marking with, or prefer us to propose a tenant-mapped VLAN scheme?

Next steps / owner: 
- Helios ops (Maria): confirm SR-IOV/NIC model and egress limits by 2026-08-26
- Jonas: produce an admission-control (AC) snippet and kube-adm hooks for the canary (due 2026-08-27)
- Karthik: run a quick SLO-to-GPU mapping sanity script and post numbers to the Drive link (due 2026-08-26)

Maria — if those baseline numbers look off for any tenant, call them out and we can re-balance. Intend to run a 2-hour canary traffic test next Tue/Wed once Helios confirms the infra.

Thanks,

Hannah

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear summary. On our side:
- Fleet details: 8x 100GbE Mellanox ConnectX-6 per host, SR-IOV enabled. Hosts are dual-socket with 2x A100-40GB GPUs.
- Egress: our colo provides 40Gbps shared egress per rack, will require shaping at the ToR if aggregate approaches that. We have a firewall appliance that supports DSCP-based policing but we prefer not to add complex ACLs unless needed.
- VLANs: we have an existing tenant VLAN mapping for production; we'll share the mapping. Agree DSCP EF for Gold, AF41 for Silver, AF21 for Bronze.

A few clarifications: for Gold sustained 500 infer/sec — is that per-tenant or per-customer-group? Also please confirm if the autoscale warmup keeps 1 instance per Gold tenant for fast recovery (we prefer a small warm pool).

We can confirm hardware and push the VLAN map by EOD Wed 2026-08-26. For the canary window, we're available Tue 2026-08-31 00:00-04:00 UTC.

Regards,
Maria

Subject: Re: Multiplex tenancy QoS & SLA matrix — VPC/private GPU handoff

Thanks — great detail, Maria. A couple of technical notes / proposals from infra: 

1) Admission control + prewarm model: we will ship a kube admission-controller hook that maps incoming tenant headers to a token bucket and consults a centralized policy. For warm pool: we recommend holding a soft warm-slot per Gold tenant (a lightweight container that keeps the KV cache warm and the model loaded but not accepting new sessions until warmed) — this reduces cold-start P95 by ~60%.

2) Network QoS shaping: with 100GbE and SR-IOV, VF-level policing + ToR shaping is the right mix. We'll add a host-level qdisc rule to prioritize DSCP EF for Gold flows. We also propose explicit egress caps per-tenant in the kube CNI so a single tenant can't saturate the host's NIC even if aggregate is high.

3) Batching and batching window: for Gold we should aim for an adaptive batching target (12-16 tokens/rt) with latency-aware fallbacks. Karthik will instrument a simulation script that maps p95 token budget to GPU slots.

Action items (internal):
- Jonas: push AC webhook and QoS proof-of-concept to the canary branch (PR by 2026-08-27)
- Karthik: run simulation + post per-tenant GPU mapping numbers to Drive (by 2026-08-26)
- Olga: prepare a short runbook for node-level troubleshooting (cache evictions, VF exhaustion) and attach to the canary doc (by 2026-08-28)

I'll prepare the AC snippet and include a fallback policy that gracefully rejects Bronze traffic when Gold cross threshold, rather than global backpressure.

Cheers,
Jonas

Maria / team — quick numbers posted to the Drive link (see related_links). Summary:
- Using the model + batch profile in the spreadsheet, 1 A100 (40GB) can sustain ~1.6k infer/sec for Bronze-like traffic (small tokens) but only ~420 infer/sec for Gold profile (longer outputs + lower batching).
- Mapping: 1 Gold tenant -> reserve 1 GPU slot (32-concurrency slot) under sustained load; pool sizing for 10 Gold tenants = 12 GPUs (includes 20% headroom)
- Network wiring: with your reported ToR 40Gbps rack egress, plan to limit aggregate cross-rack egress to 32Gbps during heavy bursts; will put this as a ToR shaping doc in the Drive.

Canary schedule accepted. I'll be online for the test window and will coordinate the PRs / scripts. Proposed canary checklist (short):
- Confirm SR-IOV + VF counts on canary hosts
- Deploy AC webhook + QoS polices in canary namespace only
- Run traffic generator with mixed tenant profile for 2 hours, step bursts + long tail sampling
- Collect p50/p95/p99 token latencies and GPU util traces, then run the postmortem template

We should be conservative on Bronze eviction during the first run. If Helios prefers, we can start with Bronze as strictly best-effort and not evict until Gold sustained for >10m.

Karthik
